title: From real activity to capability-covering robot tasks
subtitle: Trace 52,512 activity descriptions through action expansion, action deduplication, capability clustering, and three constrained k1–k5 portfolios.
goal: Select a small set of simulation action groups whose robot and physics capabilities cover as much modeled economic activity, strategic work, STEM/research, occupational diversity, and personal life as possible.
environmentDefinition: The selection unit is a final physical-action group. A selected action supplies capabilities; a target action is covered only when all requirements active in the chosen mode are supplied at or above their thresholds.
executionStatus: The source, action, value, capability, clustering, and optimization artifacts shown here are completed recorded releases. The semantic labels and merge decisions are model-produced and remain auditable in the linked files.
methodBoundary: Coverage is defined on the current action and capability graphs. Broader–narrower action relations, such as kick-ball being a subtype of strike-ball, are not yet represented and therefore do not transfer value.
walkthroughTitle: Follow one sports action through all five stages
walkthroughIntro: A broad paid-work sports description expands into “strike a sports ball or practice target.” The rows show how that action receives value and capabilities, and why it can remain uncovered.

stages.title: Collect and weight real activities
stages.question: Which parts of work and everyday life should the benchmark represent?
stages.description: Collect public activity descriptions, retain their provenance, and keep economic value and personal time as separate axes.
stages.startsWith: O*NET occupational tasks, ATUS activities, and source-native international occupation and time-use descriptions.
stages.operation: Build one traceable source record per description and attach U.S. work-value or population-time estimates where available.
stages.produces: 52,512 source activity records: 19,261 U.S. weighted records and 33,251 international records.
stages.nextStep: Expand each U.S. description into concrete robot-relevant physical actions.
stages.result: The pipeline begins from observed activity descriptions rather than a hand-written robotics task list.

stages.title: Expand descriptions into physical actions
stages.question: What externally observable robot actions are contained in each description?
stages.description: Use a complete source-level pass to recover concrete atomic actions, including valid operations implied by broad activities.
stages.operation: Classify physical content, expand supported ordinary procedures, and run a bounded recall audit on disagreements.
stages.produces: 31,961 source-specific atomic action occurrences from 9,340 action-bearing descriptions.
stages.nextStep: Map repeated or equivalent occurrences into stable action groups.
stages.result: Broad descriptions become concrete start-state-to-end-state physical operations with source provenance.

workedExample.title: The sports-practice description expands into six actions
workedExample.intro: The expansion is intentionally more concrete than the source sentence.

rows.label: Action 1
rows.value: lower the body into a squat position

rows.label: Action 2
rows.value: extend the body from a squat position to standing

rows.label: Actions 3–4
rows.value: lift and lower exercise weight or athletic equipment

rows.label: Actions 5–6
rows.value: strike a sports ball or practice target; catch a sports ball or athletic item

terms.definition: One physical operation recovered from one source context.
A concrete physical operation supported by the ordinary execution of a broad source activity.
A bounded second pass over sources where the new decomposition unexpectedly removed prior physical content.
A source description for which at least one robot-relevant external physical action was recovered.

stages.executionNote: The expansion records model-generated interpretations and evidence bases. It is deliberately broader than literal verb extraction.

substeps.title: Decompose every source
substeps.description: Produce ordered atomic actions with objects, effectors, start states, end states, and support.
substeps.input: All 19,261 U.S. source descriptions.
substeps.output: A source decomposition and zero or more atomic actions for every source.
substeps.example: The broad practice task yields a specific striking operation among five other actions.

criteria.label: External change
criteria.text: Require an observable physical or sensing result.

criteria.label: Atomicity
criteria.text: Separate operations with distinct physical end states.

criteria.label: Recall
criteria.text: Do not discard valid operations merely because the source is broad.

criteria.label: Provenance
criteria.text: Keep source text, support, object, effector, and states.

substeps.title: Run the bounded recall audit
substeps.description: Recheck every prior-physical source that the new pass classified as having no physical action.
substeps.input: 61 old-physical/new-empty disagreements.
substeps.output: 56 recovered action-bearing sources and five confirmed empty sources.
substeps.example: No recall override was needed for the sports-practice source because six actions were already recovered.

criteria.label: Scope
criteria.text: Review only the frozen disagreement set.

criteria.label: Source fidelity
criteria.text: Use the complete source description.

criteria.label: Recovery
criteria.text: Replace the base result only when the audit finds supported actions.

criteria.label: Audit trail
criteria.text: Record base and recall-audit prompt hashes.

stages.title: Deduplicate occurrences into action groups
stages.question: Which source-specific actions are the same simulation-level physical operation?
stages.description: Reuse audited groups where possible, compare new actions, and retain a lossless occurrence-to-group map.
stages.operation: Match against existing groups, independently confirm reuse, adjudicate new-action equivalence, and form final equivalence classes.
stages.produces: 9,363 action groups: 6,144 reused groups and 3,219 new corrected groups.
stages.nextStep: Attach robot and physics requirements to each action group.
stages.result: Every occurrence appears exactly once in the final group map; action value is not used to decide equivalence.

workedExample.title: Striking and kicking expose an ontology boundary
workedExample.intro: The current catalog represents equality, not broader–narrower action relations.

rows.label: Broad group
rows.value: strike a sports ball or practice target

rows.label: Specific group
rows.value: Kick a soccer ball

rows.label: Current relation
rows.value: Separate groups; kicking is a subtype of striking, not an equality relation

rows.label: Consequence
rows.value: Value aggregates within an equivalence group but does not flow from a broader action to a narrower subtype

terms.definition: An equivalence class used as the selection unit.
Assigning a recovered occurrence to an independently confirmed existing group.
The same simulation-level operation under role-preserving asset or parameter replacement.
A subtype relation such as kick-ball ⊂ strike-ball; the current action-group graph does not encode it.

stages.executionNote: The final release groups actions only through confirmed old-group reuse or confirmed new-action equivalence. It does not merge existing old groups with one another.

substeps.title: Retrieve and confirm existing groups
substeps.description: Compare each recovered action to plausible existing groups and confirm proposed reuse independently.
substeps.input: 31,961 recovered occurrences and the prior action-group catalog.
substeps.output: 6,144 reused group identities plus unmatched new-action occurrences.
substeps.example: Previously cataloged catch-ball and throw-ball actions reuse their existing groups.

decisionMethod.heading: Reuse only a physically equivalent existing group

criteria.label: Candidate retrieval
criteria.text: Retrieve physically plausible prior groups.

criteria.label: Mechanics
criteria.text: Compare effectors, contacts, state change, and success condition.

criteria.label: Confirmation
criteria.text: Require an independent reuse decision.

criteria.label: Fail closed
criteria.text: Leave unmatched actions for new-action comparison.

substeps.title: Adjudicate new-action equivalence
substeps.description: Compare unmatched actions and retain only independently confirmed equivalence edges.
substeps.input: New action occurrences and their semantic candidates.
substeps.output: 2,209 accepted and 1,142 rejected new-action equivalence edges.
substeps.example: Text similarity alone cannot merge a tool strike with a mechanically different action.

decisionMethod.heading: Use simulation equivalence rather than lexical similarity

criteria.label: Preconditions
criteria.text: Compare the initial physical relation.

criteria.label: Interaction
criteria.text: Compare active parts, contacts, and ordered physical change.

criteria.label: Outcome
criteria.text: Require the same success predicate.

criteria.label: Confirmation
criteria.text: Use only independently confirmed edges.

substeps.title: Build final action groups
substeps.description: Materialize equivalence components while preserving every occurrence and source link.
substeps.input: Confirmed existing-group matches and confirmed new-action edges.
substeps.output: 9,363 action groups and a 31,961-row occurrence map.
substeps.example: The broad sports strike receives its own stable action-group ID.

criteria.label: Losslessness
criteria.text: Assign every occurrence exactly once.

criteria.label: No value leakage
criteria.text: Do not use economic value during matching.

criteria.label: Stable identity
criteria.text: Preserve confirmed old group IDs.

criteria.label: Provenance
criteria.text: Retain source, evidence, states, and reuse decisions.

substeps.title: Apply robot eligibility
substeps.description: Exclude internal-human biological actions and quarantine the sealed holdout before selection.
substeps.input: 9,363 final action groups.
substeps.output: 9,354 eligible groups and nine sealed-holdout quarantines.
substeps.example: External sports-ball manipulation remains eligible.

criteria.label: External result
criteria.text: Keep external manipulation, sensing, and movement.

criteria.label: Internal biology
criteria.text: Exclude internal-human-only physiological actions.

criteria.label: Ambiguity
criteria.text: Default ambiguous external results to eligible.

criteria.label: Holdout
criteria.text: Do not evaluate the sealed holdout.

stages.title: Attach, deduplicate, and cluster capabilities
stages.question: Which robot and physics requirements let one selected action cover another?
stages.description: Label every action with requirement levels, conservatively deduplicate capability names, and iteratively cluster them into higher-level families.
stages.startsWith: 9,363 eligible or quarantined action groups with source provenance.
stages.operation: Generate robot and physics requirements, build canonical capabilities, map values and policy views, then run four semantic clustering rounds.
stages.produces: A thresholded action-to-capability coverage graph at every clustering round.
stages.nextStep: Optimize fixed-budget portfolios against economic and policy coverage.
stages.result: The active vocabulary contracts from 11,543 leaf nodes to 2,490 round-4 family nodes while action requirements remain traceable to their leaves.

workedExample.title: The broad sports strike becomes a capability bundle
workedExample.intro: Round 4 preserves separate robot and physics requirements and their threshold levels.

rows.label: Robot requirements
rows.value: rotational alignment, orientation control, end-effector velocity control, dynamic arm trajectory control

rows.label: Physics requirements
rows.value: momentum transfer and contact restitution

rows.label: Economic value
rows.value: $96.815M assigned to the broad strike action group

rows.label: Coverage test
rows.value: Every active-mode requirement must be supplied at an equal or higher level

terms.definition: A conservatively deduplicated robot or physics requirement.
The relative threshold that a selected action must meet or exceed.
A higher-level semantic cluster retaining links to its canonical leaves.
A capability appearing in the eligible action coverage model.

stages.executionNote: Capability clustering changes only the capability abstraction. Action groups, values, eligibility, policy units, budgets, and solver settings remain fixed across rounds.

substeps.title: Generate and conservatively deduplicate capabilities
substeps.description: Assign open-ended robot and physics requirements, then merge only complete-link confirmed capability profiles.
substeps.input: 9,363 action groups.
substeps.example: The sports strike receives both control requirements and contact/momentum requirements.

criteria.label: Separate domains
criteria.text: Keep robot and physics capabilities distinct.

criteria.label: Open vocabulary
criteria.text: Do not force actions into a fixed capability list.

criteria.label: Levels
criteria.text: Record relative requirement thresholds.

criteria.label: Complete link
criteria.text: Merge only when every required profile pair is confirmed equivalent.

substeps.title: Build action values and policy views
substeps.description: Aggregate source allocations into action values and connect actions to occupations, SOC groups, strategic domains, STEM, and personal life.
substeps.input: Source mass, final action groups, capability links, and eligibility.
substeps.example: The broad sports strike receives $96.815M from its paid-work source; the separate kick group retains personal-time value only.

decisionMethod.heading: Keep source value and policy membership traceable

criteria.label: Source conservation
criteria.text: Allocate no more than the frozen source physical mass.

criteria.label: Separate axes
criteria.text: Keep dollars and personal hours separate.

criteria.label: Policy views
criteria.text: Build occupation, SOC, strategic, STEM, and personal units.

criteria.label: No selection feedback
criteria.text: Do not use future portfolio choices to change values.

substeps.title: Iteratively cluster capabilities
substeps.description: Group semantically related active nodes in bounded cases and materialize a new capability graph after each pass.
substeps.input: 11,543 active robot and physics leaf nodes.
substeps.example: Specific motion-control labels can become a shared high-level node while retaining their leaf provenance.

decisionMethod.heading: Reduce vocabulary without changing action/value inputs

criteria.label: Bounded cases
criteria.text: Limit each semantic grouping case.

criteria.label: Same domain
criteria.text: Never merge robot with physics nodes.

criteria.label: Definition
criteria.text: Author a common capability name and definition.

criteria.label: Traceability
criteria.text: Retain every leaf ID and action incidence.

substeps.title: Remap action requirements
substeps.description: Replace leaf requirements with their active family nodes and remap direct equivalence edges.
substeps.input: One clustering round's family graph and the frozen leaf requirements.
substeps.output: A complete action-requirement table for constrained selection.
substeps.example: The broad strike remains one target action with six round-4 requirements.

criteria.label: Leaf mapping
criteria.text: Map each leaf to exactly one active node.

criteria.label: Levels
criteria.text: Preserve the maximum applicable threshold.

criteria.label: Direct edges
criteria.text: Remap direct equivalence without transitive closure.

criteria.label: Action identity
criteria.text: Do not alter action IDs or values.

stages.title: Select k1–k5 action portfolios
stages.question: Which 100 actions maximize economic and policy coverage under each capability mode?
stages.description: Run the frozen Gym-Anything tier sequence in physics-only, combined, and robotics-only modes.
stages.startsWith: Eligible action groups, thresholded capabilities, values, policy units, and a fixed 100-slot budget.
stages.operation: Solve exact joint MILPs for k1 and k2, then frozen least-covered round-robin fills for k3–k5.
stages.produces: Three auditable 100-action portfolios per complete round, with coverage snapshots, missing requirements, and leave-one-out criticality.
stages.nextStep: Use the portfolio explorer to inspect selected actions, covered targets, and remaining gaps.
stages.result: At round 4, robotics-only covers 86.73% of modeled economic mass, physics-only 83.22%, and combined 66.33%.

workedExample.title: The broad sports strike is valuable but not selected in round 4
workedExample.intro: Selection depends on marginal portfolio coverage, not direct action value alone.

terms.definition: An action whose every active-mode requirement is supplied by the selected set.
An identical or directly equivalent capability at an equal or greater requirement level.
A batch optimization that can select complementary actions together.
The policy reason an action entered the portfolio; it may improve every coverage view.

stages.executionNote: Existing simulations are not mandatory, rewarded, penalized, or read during selection. Joint k1/k2 batches are unordered; k3–k5 preserve their sequential selection order.

substeps.title: Freeze coverage, modes, and budgets
substeps.description: Define all-requirements coverage, three capability modes, and the 20/20/20/23/9/8 tier allocation.
substeps.input: Round-specific action requirements and the fixed value/policy model.
substeps.example: The sports strike is covered only if every requirement in the chosen mode is supplied.

criteria.label: Coverage
criteria.text: Require every active-mode capability threshold.

criteria.label: Modes
criteria.text: Run physics-only, combined, and robotics-only separately.

criteria.label: Budget
criteria.text: Fix 100 total selections.

criteria.label: Solver
criteria.text: Use deterministic HiGHS settings with zero MIP gap.

substeps.title: k1 — economic core
substeps.description: Jointly choose 20 eligible positive-value actions that maximize total covered economic mass.
substeps.input: All eligible positive-work-value candidates.
substeps.example: A lower-value candidate may enter if its capabilities jointly cover many higher-value targets.

criteria.label: Primary
criteria.text: Maximize newly covered economic mass.

criteria.label: Complementarity
criteria.text: Allow capabilities to be supplied by different selected actions.

criteria.label: Conditioning
criteria.text: Start from an empty selected set.

criteria.label: Tie-break
criteria.text: Minimize stable action-group indices at the optimum.

substeps.title: k2.1 — strategic domains
substeps.description: Add 20 actions maximizing the minimum coverage across healthcare, education, protective services, and transportation.
substeps.input: The frozen k1 portfolio and strategic-domain candidates.
substeps.example: Already covered strategic requirements consume no additional slot.

criteria.label: Primary
criteria.text: Maximize the least-covered strategic domain.

criteria.label: Secondary
criteria.text: Maximize total normalized strategic coverage.

criteria.label: Conditioning
criteria.text: Preserve all capabilities supplied by k1.

criteria.label: Tie-break
criteria.text: Use stable action-group indices.

substeps.title: k2.2 — STEM and research
substeps.description: Add 20 actions maximizing the minimum coverage across three STEM/research occupation groups.
substeps.input: The frozen k1+k2.1 portfolio and STEM/research candidates.
substeps.example: Architecture/engineering, computing/mathematics, and science are balanced by a maximin objective.

criteria.label: Primary
criteria.text: Maximize the least-covered STEM group.

criteria.label: Secondary
criteria.text: Maximize total normalized STEM coverage.

criteria.label: Conditioning
criteria.text: Preserve all earlier capability supply.

criteria.label: Tie-break
criteria.text: Use stable action-group indices.

substeps.title: k3 — SOC-major diversity
substeps.description: Sequentially add 23 actions from the currently least-covered SOC major group.
substeps.input: The frozen k1+k2 portfolio and 22 SOC-major policy units.
substeps.example: After every selection, coverage is recomputed before choosing the next SOC group.

criteria.label: Unit choice
criteria.text: Choose the least-covered SOC with a candidate.

criteria.label: Unit tie-break
criteria.text: Prefer larger uncovered economic mass.

criteria.label: Candidate gain
criteria.text: Maximize marginal economic coverage within that SOC.

criteria.label: Global tie-break
criteria.text: Prefer larger global economic gain.

substeps.title: k4 — niche occupations
substeps.description: Add nine actions concentrated in exactly one economic-value occupation, processing least-covered occupations first.
substeps.input: The frozen earlier portfolio and niche occupation candidates.
substeps.example: Broadly reused actions cannot displace a specialized single-occupation candidate in this tier.

criteria.label: Niche rule
criteria.text: Require provenance in exactly one valued occupation.

criteria.label: Unit choice
criteria.text: Choose the least-covered occupation.

criteria.label: Candidate gain
criteria.text: Maximize marginal coverage inside that occupation.

criteria.label: Global tie-break
criteria.text: Prefer larger global economic gain.

substeps.title: k5 — capability-family fill
substeps.description: Add eight actions to the currently least-covered capability family with attainable gain.
substeps.input: The frozen k1–k4 portfolio and active capability-family incidence.
substeps.example: This final tier targets structural holes not captured by economic or occupation views.

criteria.label: Family choice
criteria.text: Choose the least-covered family with attainable gain.

criteria.label: Candidate gain
criteria.text: Maximize newly supplied family incidence.

criteria.label: Economic tie-break
criteria.text: Prefer larger marginal global economic coverage.

criteria.label: Stable tie-break
criteria.text: Use action-group index.

substeps.title: Audit coverage and criticality
substeps.description: Recompute every target's coverage, record missing requirements, and remove each selected action once to measure its unique contribution.
substeps.input: The final 100-action portfolio for each mode.
substeps.output: Target coverage, policy-unit coverage, family coverage, cross-mode overlap, and leave-one-out criticality.
substeps.example: The sports strike record names its exact missing requirements instead of merely reporting that it was not selected.

criteria.label: Targets
criteria.text: Recompute all 9,363 action targets.

criteria.label: Missing set
criteria.text: Record each unsupplied threshold.

criteria.label: Policy views
criteria.text: Aggregate economic, strategic, STEM, SOC, occupation, and personal coverage.

criteria.label: Criticality
criteria.text: Measure coverage lost when each selected action is removed.

capabilityClustering.domainRule: Robot and physics nodes are clustered separately.
capabilityClustering.invariant: Only capability abstraction changes across rounds; actions, values, policy units, eligibility, budgets, and solver settings remain fixed.

tierBudgets.label: Economic core
tierBudgets.targetView: All economic_value policy units aggregated without double-counting their separately sourced action allocations.

tierBudgets.method: Exact joint MILP conditioned on every earlier selection.

tierBudgets.method: Exact joint MILP conditioned on every earlier selection.

tierBudgets.label: SOC-major diversity
tierBudgets.method: Sequential frozen round-robin conditioned on every earlier selection.

tierBudgets.label: Capability-family fill
tierBudgets.method: Sequential least-covered-family fill conditioned on every earlier selection.
tierBudgets.targetView: All final action-group requirement incidences in the mode; each action contributes total unit weight divided equally across its active-mode requirements.

modes.label: Physics only
modes.description: Only physics requirements determine whether a target action is covered.

modes.label: Physics + robotics
modes.description: Every physics and robot requirement must be supplied.

modes.label: Robotics only
modes.description: Only robot-control, sensing, and manipulation requirements define coverage.

selection.coverageRule: An action is covered when every requirement in the mode is supplied by at least one selected action at an equal or greater level. Different selected actions may supply different requirements.
selection.supplyRule: Supply uses the identical or one directly confirmed equivalent capability. No transitive equivalence closure is used.
selection.solver: HiGHS, zero relative and absolute MIP gap, one thread, deterministic seed.
selection.axisWarning: Economic value and personal time remain separate. Portfolio coverage is capability-mediated; direct action value alone does not determine selection.

views.label: Selected 100
views.description: Actions entering the chosen mode's portfolio.

views.label: Covered targets
views.description: All actions whose active requirements are supplied.

views.label: Coverage gaps
views.description: Unselected targets with one or more missing requirements.

views.label: Economic value
views.description: Positive modeled U.S. work value, descending.
